task_metadata.research_topic: convolutional neural network architecture design for MNIST digit classification
task_metadata.research_question: Can a better neural network architecture than the default PyTorch MNIST CNN improve MNIST accuracy under the fixed 14-epoch Adadelta training pipeline?
notes: The default baseline is linked approximately to the LeNet-style CNN literature because the shipped PyTorch example is a modernized two-convolution MNIST classifier rather than an exact reproduction of LeNet-5.
The fixed scheduler is StepLR, but no single canonical paper is cited for that implementation detail.

tests.label: train
tests.notes: The train command evaluates MNIST classification with a LeNet-style CNN, dropout regularization, and the fixed Adadelta-based training recipe.

baselines.name: default
baselines.notes: The default network is best described as a modernized LeNet-style MNIST convnet with dropout, not an exact LeNet-5 implementation.

baselines.name: batchnorm
baselines.notes: This baseline explicitly inserts BatchNorm layers into the MNIST CNN.

papers.title: Gradient-based learning applied to document recognition
papers.bibtex: @article{Lecun_1998, title={Gradient-based learning applied to document recognition}, volume={86}, ISSN={0018-9219}, url={http://dx.doi.org/10.1109/5.726791}, DOI={10.1109/5.726791}, number={11}, journal={Proceedings of the IEEE}, publisher={Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE)}, author={Lecun, Y. and Bottou, L. and Bengio, Y. and Haffner, P.}, year={1998}, pages={2278–2324} }
papers.relevance: Foundational LeNet-style MNIST paper and the closest literature match for the task's default CNN baseline and benchmark.

papers.title: Batch Normalization: Accelerating Deep Network Training by Reducing Internal Covariate Shift
papers.relevance: Direct paper match for the explicit BatchNorm architecture baseline provided in the task stub.

papers.title: Improving neural networks by preventing co-adaptation of feature detectors
papers.relevance: The shipped PyTorch MNIST model uses dropout layers, so this paper is part of the task's fixed training/architecture recipe.

papers.title: ADADELTA: An Adaptive Learning Rate Method
papers.relevance: The task description fixes Adadelta as the optimizer, making this paper directly relevant to the scaffold all agents must use.

papers.title: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition
papers.relevance: Residual connections are a standard architecture modification that could plausibly transfer to compact MNIST CNN redesigns under this task.

papers.title: Densely Connected Convolutional Networks
papers.relevance: Dense connectivity is another transferable architecture idea relevant to the task's mandate to improve a small CNN by structural changes.

papers.title: Very Deep Convolutional Networks for Large-Scale Image Recognition
papers.relevance: VGG-style use of repeated small convolutions is directly relevant when redesigning the fixed small MNIST CNN for better accuracy.

papers.title: Highway Networks
papers.relevance: Highway-style gating is a relevant predecessor to residual-style architecture improvements for deeper CNNs.

papers.title: Network In Network
papers.relevance: Network In Network proposes stronger local nonlinear modeling and global average pooling, both reasonable architecture directions for this task.

papers.title: EfficientNet: Rethinking Model Scaling for Convolutional Neural Networks
papers.relevance: EfficientNet is relevant because the task asks for architecture changes under a fixed training budget, making parameter-efficient scaling ideas pertinent.
